thread:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — service degradation detected for hosted inference (us-west-2). Elevated 5xx rate and tail latency starting ~22:08 UTC. Pager triggered for oncall team :rotating_light:

Jordan (oncall): saw it. investigating now. tracing requests -> errors spiking on the frontend gateway. digging into recent deploys.

Maya R.: looping in infra, I can help with capacity scaling if it's a scheduling/queue issue. Jordan, any evidence of a bad model or kernel failure?

Jordan (oncall): not yet. stack traces show `kv-cache` timeouts and a bunch of `OOM` logs from a worker pod cluster. attaching snippets:

```
2026-02-18T22:09:12Z worker-47 ERROR OOM when allocating 4.2G
2026-02-18T22:09:12Z gateway WARN downstream request 500 curl_id=abc123
```

deploy-bot: Recent deploy at 22:01 UTC: `model-serving:release-2026-02-18` (canary -> prod).

Priya S.: paging infra and runtime owners. I'm going to remove canary traffic from prod and scale up dedicated-pool-2. Also enabling fallback to quantized variant for high mem models.

Jordan (oncall): proceeding with two mitigations: 1) revert canary traffic routing (command below), 2) bump replica count on worker nodes for us-west-2 for next 30m.

```
# revert canary
redwoodctl routing set --env prod --model all --policy default
# scale pool
redwoodctl pool scale --name dedicated-pool-2 --replicas +6
```

Maya R.: started scale. also enabling prefix caching for repeated requests as quick mitigation.

Alex M.: heads-up to support: customers may see timeouts, please hold public statements until we know impact.

Sam - Finance: tagging onto this — we will need a customer impact summary if SLA credits are required. Please collect affected tenant list, start/end times, and estimated token/service hours so finance can calculate credits.

Jordan (oncall): confirmed canary rollback succeeded at 22:17 UTC; error rate falling. scaling completed 22:20 UTC. monitoring for 15m. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — degraded -> partial recovery. severity lowered.

Priya S.: keeping fallback quantized models as live policy for next 2 hours to avoid recurrence. Will run heap-checks on nodes.

Alex M.: marking incident for postmortem. assigning owners for remediation.

Jordan (oncall): Proposed postmortem agenda and owners:
- Timeline & root cause analysis (Jordan)
- Capacity/Autoscale improvements (Maya)
- Deploy gating and canary controls (Eng/Deploy team)
- Billing/customer impact + SLA calc (Sam - Finance)

Maya R.: action item: add pre-deploy memory regression test into CI and tighten canary traffic ramp (target < 5% for 30m). ETA: 2026-02-25 EOD.

Jordan (oncall): action item: add log correlation and earlier OOM alert rule, threshold at 3 OOMs in 5m. ETA: 2026-02-22.

Sam - Finance: For SLA calculations, I need per-tenant usage during 22:05–22:25 UTC. Also need whether this qualifies under SLA window (hosted API, standard tier) and whether multiple incidents counted. I'll prepare a draft credit schedule once I have the list.

Alex M.: list of customers that reported timeouts so far: acme-corp, betaapps, edu-portal. Jordan, can you confirm request counts and affected endpoints for those?

Jordan (oncall): pulling logs now. preliminary: acme-corp ~1200 requests failed in window, betaapps ~430, edu-portal ~95. Mostly generation endpoints `/v1/generate` with long-context models.

Priya S.: note — two of those tenants were routed to dedicated-pool-2; we'll need pool-hour accounting for the cost impact.

Sam - Finance: thanks. Finance needs the following to proceed with credits and billing adjustments:
1) A CSV with tenant_id, tenant_name, start_ts, end_ts, failed_requests, total_requests, estimated_tokens_lost, invoice_account_id.
2) Confirmation of SLA terms triggered (percent uptime impact).
3) Any contractual exceptions or waivers (legal/compliance).

Jordan (oncall): I'll export CSV and drop into /shared/incidents/1823456789/impact.csv and ping you when ready. ETA 2h.

Maya R.: schedule postmortem review: suggested 2026-02-20 16:00 UTC. Is that ok for finance to join?

Sam - Finance: can do 16:00 UTC. please include calendar invite + dial-in.

Alex M.: adding follow-up ask for invoicing team: if SLA credit is approved, we prefer a credit on next invoice rather than a retro refund. Sam, confirm if that's doable.

Sam - Finance: default is invoice credit in next billing cycle. If enterprise customer requests cash refund, route to billing ops + legal. Will confirm after calculations.

Jordan (oncall): impact.csv uploaded: https://files.redwood/internal/incidents/1823456789/impact.csv (contains anonymized tenant ids).

Sam - Finance: got it. Starting calculation. Quick estimate: based on token-hours and SLA table, provisional credit range is 5–10% of monthly usage for impacted tenants depending on exact outage minutes. I'll post a formal breakdown by EOD.

Priya S.: remediation checklist created and added to runbook: `/runbooks/serving/oom-mitigation` — includes steps we took and permanent fixes planned.

Maya R.: I'll open a tracking epic and link action items. Epic: REDWOOD-INC-182345 (owners: Maya/Jordan).

Alex M.: request to support: draft customer communication for affected tenants (hold for legal review). Template in `/templates/incident_customer_notice.md` — please prepare and drop in the postmortem doc.

Sam - Finance: once I have final numbers, I'll create a billing ADJ ticket and CC accounting: ticket BILL-5078. Expect follow-up in 3 business days with proposed credits and invoice notes.

Jordan (oncall): postmortem meeting scheduled and invite sent. I'll lead RCA and timeline.

Priya S.: closing incident thread — monitor for 2 more hours then will archive. Great teamwork everyone. :tada: 

Sam - Finance: noted. After postmortem, finance will need the final confirmed timeline and any approved remediation that changes SLA terms.

Alex M.: marking completed immediate mitigation. leaving open actions for tracking in REDWOOD-INC-182345.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — all mitigation steps applied. Follow-ups open for postmortem and billing reconciliation.
